name: New Orleans
operatingHours: RTA streetcars: St. Charles (12) runs 24 h, every ~12–15 min by day and ~30 min overnight; the Canal lines (47 City Park/Museum, 48 Cemeteries) ~4:30 AM–~2:30 AM, every ~11 min on the shared Canal Street section; Riverfront and Rampart–St. Claude ~6:00 AM–~12:00 AM, every ~20–30 min. Times are approximate; check the Le Pass app for live arrivals.
fareInfo: $1.25 a ride on streetcars and buses (exact cash only, no change), with free transfers within 2 hours when paying in the Le Pass app. Jazzy Pass 1-day $3, 3-day $8, 7-day $15, 31-day $45, sold in the Le Pass app, at Canal Street machines and at Walgreens; children under 5 ride free. Jazzy Passes also cover buses and the Canal Street ferry.

sights.name: The National WWII Museum
sights.note: A sprawling Warehouse District campus that tells the story of the Second World War through aircraft halls, personal testimony and an immersive 4D film.

sights.name: Frenchmen Street
sights.note: Three Marigny blocks of small clubs where local brass, jazz and funk bands play from early evening until late, with an art market at night.
sights.hours: Street always open; clubs ~5:00 PM–~2:00 AM, busiest Thu–Sat

sights.name: Preservation Hall
sights.note: A tiny, unadorned hall on St. Peter Street devoted to traditional New Orleans jazz, played acoustically in short sets to a seated crowd.

sights.name: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1
sights.note: The city's oldest surviving cemetery, a maze of above-ground tombs including the reputed resting place of voodoo priestess Marie Laveau.
sights.hours: Guided tours only, daily ~9:00 AM–4:00 PM starts; some Saturday evening tours

sights.name: Mardi Gras World
sights.note: A riverside working studio where guided tours show the giant floats and sculpted props built for Carnival parades.
sights.hours: Daily ~9:30 AM–4:30 PM, tours every ~30 min

sights.name: Jackson Square
sights.note: The French Quarter's historic parade ground, ringed by street artists, musicians and the Pontalba buildings and framed by the cathedral.
sights.hours: Promenade always open; inner garden ~8:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: New Orleans City Park
sights.note: A huge park of moss-draped live oaks and lagoons holding the botanical garden, a vintage carousel, the art museum and its sculpture garden.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily; gardens and rides keep their own hours

sights.name: St. Louis Cathedral
sights.note: The white triple-spired cathedral at the head of Jackson Square, one of the oldest Catholic cathedrals in continuous use in the United States.
sights.hours: Daily ~8:30 AM–4:00 PM between Masses; free

sights.name: Audubon Zoo
sights.note: An Uptown zoo known for its Louisiana Swamp exhibit with white alligators, plus jaguars, orangutans and a giraffe feeding deck.

sights.name: New Orleans Pharmacy Museum
sights.note: An 1820s apothecary shop preserved with hand-blown medicine bottles, voodoo remedies and grim early surgical tools.

sights.name: Royal Street
sights.note: The Quarter's most elegant street, lined with antique dealers, galleries and wrought-iron balconies, with buskers on the pedestrian blocks by day.
sights.hours: Street always open; shops ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Audubon Aquarium
sights.note: A riverfront aquarium at the foot of Canal Street with a walk-through Caribbean reef tunnel, a Gulf of Mexico tank and the Audubon Insectarium under the same roof.

sights.name: Sydney and Walda Besthoff Sculpture Garden
sights.note: Free outdoor galleries beside the New Orleans Museum of Art where large modern sculptures sit among lagoons, oaks and footbridges.
sights.hours: Daily ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM (longer in summer); free

sights.name: Hermann-Grima House
sights.note: An 1831 Federal-style townhouse with a working open-hearth kitchen, shown on guided tours about family and enslaved life in antebellum New Orleans.
sights.hours: Wed–Mon 10:00 AM–4:00 PM, tours on the hour (none at noon); closed Tue

sights.name: The Historic New Orleans Collection
sights.note: A free museum and research center across Royal Street buildings, covering the city's history through maps, paintings and changing exhibitions.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 9:30 AM–4:30 PM, Sun 10:30 AM–4:30 PM; free

sights.name: Audubon Park
sights.note: A broad Uptown park across St. Charles Avenue from Tulane, with a loop path around lagoons full of egrets and centuries-old oaks.

sights.name: French Market
sights.note: Open-air sheds along Decatur Street with food stalls, a farmers market and craft and souvenir vendors, by the Mississippi levee.

sights.name: Crescent Park
sights.note: A free linear park on old riverside wharves from Marigny to Bywater, with skyline views of downtown across the Mississippi bend.

railStations.name: New Orleans Union Passenger Terminal
railStations.note: The city's Amtrak and Greyhound station on Loyola Avenue: City of New Orleans to Chicago, Crescent to New York via Atlanta, Sunset Limited to Los Angeles (3× weekly) and the Mardi Gras Service to Mobile. The Loyola streetcar (on the map) stops outside and reaches Canal Street in ~5 min.
railStations.hours: Station ~5:00 AM–~10:30 PM; trains to their timetables. Loyola streetcar ~6:00 AM–~12:00 AM.

airports.name: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail link. RTA's 202 Airport Express bus ($1.25, from Level 1 outside Door 2, zones B4–B5) runs every ~70–90 min to Union Passenger Terminal and Elk Place by Canal Street in ~45 min (not on the map). Jefferson Transit's E1 ($2) goes to City Park Avenue; taxis charge a flat fare to the CBD/French Quarter in ~25 min.
airports.hours: 202 Airport Express ~4:50 AM–~9:40 PM; no overnight bus.
